key_insight: Deep generative crystal structure predictors outperform only partially beyond template retrieval, and their apparent de novo ability is largely driven by prototype dependence.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials design, this means benchmarking should separate true novelty from prototype-library lookup effects before claiming generative advantage.
method: Benchmarked 12 generative CSP models across latent-variable, diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive, and manifold random-walk families.
Compared all methods with TCSP 2.0 using identical structure-matching, symmetry, and consensus criteria.
Performed leakage-controlled retraining by removing entire stoichiometric prototype families to test prototype dependence.
evidence_signal: On 180 test structures and a leakage-controlled subset of 46, template retrieval achieved 68.3% top-1 success, while the strongest generative models reached 66.4% and 62.9%; retraining caused 50–78% accuracy drops across four held-out prototype families.
watch_item: The reported gains are sensitive to prototype-family overlap, so evaluating only aggregate match rate can overstate true de novo predictive power.
paper_title: Deep Generative Crystal Structure Prediction: A Benchmark Study and a Controlled Test of Prototype Dependence
